cards.text: Jesus just told a storm to calm down, and it did (Matthew 8:26). Now He lands on the other side, in the region of the Gadarenes. And somebody is waiting for Him, friend, and it is NOT a welcome committee.

cards.question: Jesus lands in the region of the Gadarenes. Who comes to meet Him?
Where are these two demon-possessed men coming from?
The two demon-possessed men from the tombs are so ___ that no one can pass that way.

cards.text: A road so dangerous NOBODY can use it. That's not a shortcut, friend, that's a take-the-long-way-and-never-speak-of-it road.

cards.question: The two men shout at Jesus. They call Him the ___ of God.
The men shout at Jesus, the Son of God. What are they afraid He has come to do?

answers.text: Torture them before the appointed time
Chase them out of the tombs forever
Take them back across the sea

cards.text: Hold on. The disciples just asked, "What kind of man is this?" (Matthew 8:27). And the demons are out here SHOUTING the answer: Son of God.
Meanwhile, in the distance, a large herd of pigs is feeding. I'm just saying, friend. Keep an eye on those pigs.

cards.question: With a large herd of pigs feeding nearby, what do the demons beg Jesus to do if He drives them out?

answers.text: Let them stay in the tombs

cards.question: True or false: Jesus answers the demons' request with a long speech.

cards.text: "Go!" He tells them, and they come out and go into the pigs. ONE word and they're GONE, while I need three alarms just to find my apron.

cards.question: True or false: Once the demons go into the pigs, the whole herd rushes down the steep bank into the sea.

cards.text: The whole herd dies in the waters. Now picture being the guys tending those pigs, trying to explain THAT one.

cards.question: The men tending the pigs run off into the town. What do they report?

answers.text: Everything including what happened to the two men
Only that the whole herd was lost
That thieves had taken the herd away

cards.text: Then the WHOLE town goes out to meet Jesus. Everybody. Every last one.

cards.question: When the whole town sees Jesus, they beg Him to ___ their region.

cards.text: Jesus just set free two men nobody could get past. And the town looks right at Him and says, "Please. Just go."

findings.problem: "Somebody is waiting for Him" goes beyond the text. Matthew 8:28 says He was met by two demon-possessed men coming from the tombs. It never says they were waiting for Him.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "sleepy" is silly next to "violent". The clause "no one can pass that way" also rules out both "sleepy" and "quiet", so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: This story card only retells verse 8:28, which cards 1 to 4 already covered. It adds a joke but doesn't move the passage forward, so it works as a recap card.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the exact title the men use (Son, Lamb or Word). Nothing earlier lets the baker reason it out, so it tests wording they haven't seen. "Lamb" is also a real title of Jesus elsewhere, so a baker could argue for it.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: "What are they afraid He has come to do?" states a feeling as fact. Matthew 8:29 only gives their question: "Have You come here to torture us before the appointed time?"

rule.text: Feelings: He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Chase them out of the tombs forever" is close to what happens in the passage, where the demons say "If You drive us out" (8:31) and Jesus does send them out (8:32). A baker could argue it's right.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The card says "The disciples just asked", but Matthew 8:27 says "The men were amazed and asked". The text calls them "the men", not the disciples.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: "Keep an eye on those pigs" points the baker straight to the answer of card 10, which asks where the demons want to be sent. The question on card 10 then repeats the pigs again.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The joke doesn't match the action. The core action is one word and they leave at once. "Three alarms just to find my apron" mixes waking up with finding something, so it doesn't click instantly.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: "The men tending the pigs" adds a detail the text doesn't give. Matthew 8:33 says "Those tending the pigs".

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.
